prompts.band-neck-flexion:
Create one polished landscape educational exercise illustration for the existing GetFit workout app, approximately 1536x1024. Realistic softly rendered anatomical fitness illustration, cream/off-white studio background, olive green T-shirt, black shorts, adult athletic male, gentle natural light. Clean clear details rather than cinematic effects. Two panels with ample spacing and readable short Italian labels. No logo, watermark, numeric load, resistance rating, doses, approval forms or decorative objects. Neck anatomy and band routing must be physically plausible. No elastic on throat, anterior neck, eyes, nose or mouth; no heavy harness, weights, head bridges or explosive motion. Pale grey alignment guides, amber external-force arrows labeled "Trazione", deep forest-green movement arrows only when there is actual movement. Isometric exercises show stationary head with no movement arrows.
Exercise: Flessione cervicale isometrica con elastico, working anterior neck against a gentle backward pull. Both panels are a right-facing SIDE VIEW, head upright over shoulders, eyes horizontal, chin slightly tucked, torso upright. A purpose-designed broad padded headband sits around the SKULL ABOVE THE EYEBROWS, stabilized by a strap over the crown, no chin/neck straps. The forehead is supported by the padded front portion of the headband. Two elastic lengths run symmetrically BACKWARDS along the OUTSIDES of the skull from lateral attachment points to a stable gym-rack anchor BEHIND the person at forehead height (rack on LEFT of each panel). The band never passes through the skull or the face. The elastic and anchor must be unmistakable and not be a loop around the neck. Left panel label "Posizione"; right panel label "Tenuta". Same neutral head position in both; on right show a small amber arrow pointing LEFT towards the rear anchor, text "Trazione indietro". Bottom text "Testa ferma · sguardo orizzontale". Head and shoulder close-up enough for smartphone. Draw the safe headband routing with precision; no manually applied hand resistance.

Exercise: Retrazione cervicale con elastico. Two RIGHT-FACING SIDE VIEWS showing an upright man facing a sturdy vertical WALL on the RIGHT. The torso and forearms stay fixed between frames. The change is tiny, no exaggerated forward-head starting posture, no neck extension, no circular nodding arrow. Bottom text "Piccolo movimento · sguardo orizzontale". Exactly two anatomically correct arms per person.

reviewNotes: Original illustrations, not photographs of a clinical demonstration.
Neutral head for all isometric holds; no head-movement arrow.
Lateral labels refer to the working anatomical side, opposite the anchor.
Extension image edited to raise hands and elastic above the eyes, with a horizontal forward pull.
Retraction shows a small horizontal backward translation with forearms supported at the wall.
Chin nod keeps the head supported and uses no elastic.

edits.band-neck-extension: Edit this exercise illustration with one precise biomechanical correction in BOTH panels. Keep exactly the same man, cream background, two-panel composition, Italian labels, neutral stationary head, clothing and realistic illustration style. RAISE BOTH HANDS from chest height to FOREHEAD HEIGHT, with fists slightly outward so they do not obscure the face. Elbows naturally bent, forearms elevated. The TWO green band strands must run HORIZONTALLY FORWARDS from the upper OCCIPUT along the OUTSIDES of the skull ABOVE THE EARS AND EYEBROWS to these raised hands. Both strands stay above the eyes, never crossing or touching cheek, nose, mouth, eyes or throat. Their posterior contact remains behind the skull, not around the forehead; preserve the continuous two-strand route. On the right panel replace the downward diagonal traction arrows with HORIZONTAL RIGHT-POINTING amber arrows parallel to the band. Keep text 'Trazione avanti', 'Posizione', 'Tenuta' and 'Testa ferma · non guardare in alto'. Head and torso remain identical and neutral between panels, eyes horizontal. No head movement, no extra limbs, no other changes.
